title: Compatibility Exercise
prompt: Identify and resolve unsupported syntax or dependency constraints across Python versions. Build a small program, document its expected behavior, and test at least one edge case. Use only synthetic data and local files.
objective: Apply compatibility exercise to demonstrate lessons 230–324 from the supplied curriculum.

starter.code:
# Implement: Compatibility Exercise
# Requirements: Identify and resolve unsupported syntax or dependency constraints across Python versions.

expected_output: A Python program that meets the acceptance criteria for Compatibility Exercise and passes the listed checks; verify runtime behavior locally.
acceptance_criteria: The program addresses the stated task: Identify and resolve unsupported syntax or dependency constraints across Python versions.
The main logic is separated into a short, readable function when appropriate.
At least one normal input and one edge/failure case are tested.
No secrets or real personal data are included.
The result and known limitations are explained in learner-authored words.
hints: Start with the smallest version that demonstrates the expected behavior.
Test normal inputs and at least one boundary or failure case.
Write down why the result is correct; a text check alone cannot prove a program is correct.
grading_method: Repository grader performs a required-string smoke check only. This is not Python execution and does not establish runtime correctness; use local tests and human review.
retry_policy: Allow retries. Any completion and XP decision remains under the platform backend rules; this file defines no XP overrides.
status_note: Draft exercise based on Section C of Python.pdf; review starter, hidden reference solution and grading rubric before publication.
